note: Candidates reviewed for this update but not admitted, with the reason and the evidence that would reopen each.

entries.candidate: Google Henderson data center, Henderson, Clark County, NV (Jasmine Development LLC; 520 / 560 W Warm Springs Rd; Clark County parcel 178-01-416-001)
entries.reason: Google's Henderson location page in its version of 6 October 2026 (datacenters.google sitemap lastmod 2026-10-06T15:04:30-04:00; Internet Archive copies of 26 August and 9 October 2026 bound it, the only change being a new card for Google's 15 September 2026 Nevada energy fund) says 'our Henderson data center in Clark County, Nevada, is helping the region progress into a digital hub', that the Henderson and Storey County data centers 'were built in 2019 and 2021', and the locations index lists Henderson with inDevelopment false; the q3-hyperscalers-p3 sweep (sixtyeighth holds) rejected these pages as lacking a dated status statement. The locator is the open problem: the Clark County air-quality register lists JASMINE DEVELOPMENT LLC as a DATA CENTER minor source (NAICS 518210) at 520 Warm Springs Rd, Henderson, and the Accela owner layer shows Jasmine Development L L C owning parcel 178-01-416-001 at 560 W Warm Springs Rd (59.9 acres; current polygon) and parcels 178-01-415-001, 178-12-110-004 and -007 (no current polygons), with a registered-agent mailing address in Delaware. No captured official or Google source ties Jasmine Development LLC to Google; City of Henderson hosts (www.cityofhenderson.com, maps.cityofhenderson.com) return HTTP 403 to robots.txt. Not in the Atlas.
entries.reopen_condition: An official or Google record naming Google (or Google LLC) at 520 / 560 W Warm Springs Rd or as the principal of Jasmine Development LLC (for example a Clark County or City of Henderson permit or certificate of occupancy, a GOED abatement record, or a PUCN filing), together with a dated in-window operating statement (the 6 October 2026 page version stays within 85 days until 30 December 2026); then admit with the parcel 178-01-416-001 centroid as locator.

entries.candidate: Google Storey County data center campus, Tahoe-Reno Industrial Center, Storey County, NV (candidate holding: Silver Slate LLC, about 1,210 acres)
entries.reason: Google's Storey County location page in its version of 6 October 2026 (sitemap lastmod 2026-10-06T15:02:47-04:00; Internet Archive copies of 17 July and 11 October 2026 bound it, the only change being the Nevada energy-fund card) says 'the Storey County data center works with the community to operate sustainably', that it 'was built in 2021', and that Google began using geothermal energy to power its Storey County data center campus in 2023; the index lists it with inDevelopment false. The Nevada statewide parcel layer (gis.dot.nv.gov, Division of State Lands 2018 snapshot) returns no Storey County parcel owned by Google; the only company holding of about 1,210 acres is SILVER SLATE LLC, which matches the size of Google's reported TRIC purchase but is not tied to Google by any captured official or Google source. Current Storey County parcel services are not usable (storeynv.devnetwedge.com /parcel/* disallowed; the county's hosted layers on services6.arcgis.com sit behind a robots.txt that returns HTTP 403). Not in the Atlas.
entries.reopen_condition: An official or Google record tying Google's Storey County campus to its parcels (for example a Storey County permit, special use permit, abatement or GOED record naming Google or Silver Slate LLC with APNs or an address), a usable current county parcel source, and a dated in-window operating statement (the 6 October 2026 page version stays within 85 days until 30 December 2026).

entries.candidate: Switch Citadel Campus (Tahoe Reno, Storey County, NV; SUPERNAP RENO LLC holding of about 1,007 acres in the 2018 statewide parcel layer) and Switch The Core campus, Las Vegas (7135 S Decatur Blvd area, NV LAS NAP 7 LLC)
entries.reason: Switch's Tahoe Reno page (captured 26 October 2026, dateModified 2026-10-12T19:25:16Z) and Las Vegas page (us-southwest-p2 capture of 23 October 2026, dateModified 2026-10-12T19:27:02Z) describe the Citadel Campus as one that 'will have gigawatts of power capacity upon completion, making it the world's most powerful colocation data center campus' and The Core as one that 'will have up to 495 MW of power upon completion'; neither states that a named building operates, and the 10 October 2026 re-save of Switch's 'PRIME data center locations' post is generic. The 2018 statewide parcel layer shows SUPERNAP RENO LLC holding about 1,007 acres in Storey County (Switch's former SUPERNAP brand), a usable identity lead. The Core lies about 1.9 km from the published NV LAS NAP 17 & 18 site and may need to be treated as the same campus. Not in the Atlas (except the NAP 17 & 18 site).
entries.reopen_condition: A dated Switch statement (or county record such as a certificate of occupancy or final inspection) that a named Citadel or Core building operates or is under construction, within 85 days, with a current parcel locator; for The Core, a campus-identity review against the published NV LAS NAP 17 & 18 site.

entries.candidate: Corrigan Farms data center project, Eagle Mountain, Utah County, UT (Corrigan Farms LLC; Utah County parcel 59:068:0006, 40.99 acres; RTI overlay rezone and development agreement)
entries.reason: Eagle Mountain City's Planning Commission recommended approval of the rezone and development agreement on 22 September 2026; on 6 October 2026 the City Council tabled both ordinances (minutes: the agreement was 'based on terms consistent with other data center development agreements' because 'a specific buyer had not been identified'); the 20 October 2026 agenda (posted 15 October; packet with draft agreement of 13 October) put them back for discussion and action. The staff report says the parcel 'abuts other data center properties' and that 'It is anticipated that the applicant will construct 2 data centers with an on site natural gas power plant', but the draft agreement describes a landowner entitlement for uses that 'may include' data centers, with no developer, operator or site plan, and the outcome of 20 October is not yet published. Not in the Atlas.
entries.reopen_condition: Published minutes or an adopted ordinance showing the City Council approved the Corrigan Farms rezone and development agreement, or a site plan or building permit naming a data-centre developer, with the Utah County parcel 59:068:0006 geometry as locator; admit as announced (or permitted only with an issued building or planning consent for data-centre buildings).

entries.candidate: Novva Tahoe Reno data center (Tahoe-Reno Industrial Center, Storey County, NV; 20-acre campus, six 10 MW halls)
entries.reason: Re-read 26 October 2026 (local novva-tahoe-reno-20261026.html; dateModified 2026-08-31): the page says 'Novva's Tahoe Reno facility sits on a 20-acre campus in the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center' with 180,000 sq ft of white floor space and on-site 24x7 staffing among its specifications, and calls it 'our new data center facility', but unlike the Utah page it publishes no measured water use or annualized PUE and gives no street address or APN; no usable current Storey County parcel source exists (see the Google Storey County hold). Not in the Atlas.
entries.reopen_condition: A bounded page version or dated Novva or county record stating that the Tahoe Reno facility serves customers, plus its address and a usable Storey County parcel locator.

entries.candidate: Beat sweep of permits and development agreements, 26 October 2026: Eagle Mountain, West Jordan, Lehi and Millard County (UT); Storey, Washoe and Clark counties (NV); Kuna and Ada County (ID)
entries.reason: Eagle Mountain City Council and Planning Commission agendas from 28 July to 27 October 2026 (CivicClerk API): the only data-centre item is Corrigan Farms (held above); the 20 October 2026 Will-Power UT, LLC (Williams) reimbursement agreement concerns a natural gas power plant under construction, not a data centre. West Jordan planning-commission, administrative-hearing and council hearing notices (15 July - 26 October 2026) and Lehi planning-commission hearing notices (13 August - 22 October 2026) name no data-centre application. Millard County notices (July - October 2026): zone changes Z-2026-048 (Heavy Industrial, about 323 acres near Holden), Z-2026-064 (Light Industrial, Flowell) and Z-2026-072 (Heavy Industrial, about 700 acres near Delta/Deseret, Planning Commission hearing 5 November 2026) name no data-centre use; the Joule Capital Partners development agreement Z-2026-026 (April 2026) is a 24-inch gas pipeline. Storey County BOCC packets 4 August - 20 October 2026 contain no data-centre consent (345 kV transmission and tower-height SUPs; the Fleet Data Centers gas-generator SUPs were July decisions already held). Clark County Legistar has only the NV NAP 6 LLC items on the 17 June 2026 agenda (held by us-southwest-p2). Washoe County planning pages are not updated past spring 2026; Kuna's AgendaCenter is stale; adacounty.id.gov and the City of Henderson return HTTP 403 to robots.txt.
entries.reopen_condition: New dated data-centre permits, development agreements or site plans in these registers.

entries.candidate: Flexential Las Vegas data centers (North Data Center, 3330 Lone Mountain Rd, North Las Vegas, per the Clark County air-quality register lead; Downtown Data Center), Clark County, NV
entries.reason: Not in the Atlas. www.flexential.com allows content paths in robots.txt but its sitemap returned HTTP 403 (bot protection), so the host was treated as blocked; the Internet Archive holds copies of the Las Vegas market page (latest 2 July 2026) and of the North (15 March 2026) and Downtown (14 February 2026) facility pages, all before the 85-day window, so no in-window dated page version is available.
entries.reopen_condition: An Internet Archive copy (or another dated Flexential or Clark County / City of North Las Vegas record) within 85 days stating that the North or Downtown facility operates, with the Clark County Assessor parcel at its address as locator.
